issues.legal_issue: Delay in sending an occurrence report to a magistrate does not by itself taint an investigation or make a prosecution unsupported when the first information report was recorded promptly, the investigation began on its basis, no other infirmity is shown, and no prejudice from the delay is claimed.
material_facts: The occurrence report reached the magistrate at about 6 p.m., several hours after the occurrence.
The first information report had been recorded without undue delay, and the investigation began on its basis.
No other infirmity in the investigation was brought to the Court's notice, and the accused did not claim prejudice from the delayed receipt.
issues.conclusion: The delayed receipt of the occurrence report, though improper or objectionable, did not by itself justify treating the investigation as tainted or the prosecution as unsupported.
issues.legal_principle: Section 157 of the Code of Criminal Procedure requires the police officer to send the occurrence report forthwith to a magistrate empowered to take cognizance. Its purpose is to keep the magistrate informed of the investigation and enable appropriate control or directions under section 159. Delay alone does not establish a tainted investigation or unsupported prosecution where the first information report was recorded promptly, the investigation proceeded on its basis, no other infirmity is shown, and no prejudice is claimed.

rule.if: criminal_case_with_delayed_occurrence_report and first_information_report_recorded_promptly and investigation_started_on_first_information_report and no_other_investigative_infirmity_shown and no_prejudice_from_delay_claimed

predicates.criminal_case_with_delayed_occurrence_re: The case involved a criminal investigation in which the occurrence report was sent to the magistrate late.
predicates.first_information_report_recorded_prompt: The police recorded the first information report without undue delay after the occurrence.
predicates.investigation_started_on_first_informati: The police began the investigation on the basis of the first information report.
predicates.no_other_investigative_infirmity_shown: No other infirmity in the investigation was brought to the court's notice.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_delay_claimed: The accused did not claim that the late report prejudiced them.
predicates.delay_alone_does_not_make_investigation_: The delay by itself does not make the investigation tainted or the prosecution unsupported.

issues.definition: When a criminal case involves a late occurrence report but the first report and investigation were prompt, no other investigative defect is shown, and no prejudice is claimed, the delay alone does not make the investigation tainted or the prosecution unsupported.

issues.legal_issue: Alleged alterations in an inquest report or a site plan do not by themselves make an investigation or prosecution unreliable when the surrounding circumstances and trustworthy prosecution evidence do not support a grave suspicion.
material_facts: The inquest report was sent with the deceased's body, and the evidence showed it had been prepared and dispatched promptly.

The accused alleged that a digit and a word referring to the number of injuries had been added to witness statements attached to the inquest report; the Court assumed this possibility without deciding that alterations had occurred.
The site plan referred to a conspiracy offence and an alleged participant, but the initial information already referred to that person's grievance and interest in the disputed land.
The Court found the prosecution evidence generally trustworthy.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the alleged additions to the inquest report had been made, they did not by themselves undermine its general trustworthiness or make the investigation fatally suspicious; the site-plan criticism likewise did not create grave suspicion of the prosecution story in light of the trustworthy evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the alleged irregularities in the context of the record as a whole. An assumed alteration in an inquest report does not by itself render the report generally untrustworthy or the investigation fatally suspicious; an apparent addition in a site plan likewise does not justify grave suspicion where the initial information supports the relevant background and the prosecution evidence is trustworthy.

rule.if: criminal_case_challenging_investigation_reliability and alleged_inquest_or_site_plan_irregularity and inquest_report_dispatched_promptly and initial_information_supports_site_plan_background and prosecution_evidence_trustworthy

predicates.criminal_case_challenging_investigation_: The case involved a criminal prosecution in which the accused challenged the reliability of the investigation.
predicates.alleged_inquest_or_site_plan_irregularit: The accused alleged an alteration in an inquest report or a suspicious addition to a site plan.
predicates.inquest_report_dispatched_promptly: The police dispatched the inquest report with the deceased's body without undue delay.
predicates.initial_information_supports_site_plan_b: The initial information already supported the background later recorded in the site plan.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_trustworthy: The court found the prosecution evidence generally trustworthy.
predicates.alleged_documentary_irregularity_alone_d: The alleged document irregularity, by itself, does not make the prosecution unreliable.

issues.definition: In a criminal case challenging investigative documents, a prompt dispatch, supporting initial information, and trustworthy prosecution evidence mean that an alleged documentary irregularity alone does not make the prosecution unreliable.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing an appeal against acquittal may review the entire evidence and reach its own conclusion, while taking account of the presumption of innocence, the acquittal, the trial court's reasons, and the need to explain why the acquittal was unjustified.
material_facts: The State appealed against the trial court's acquittal.

The High Court examined the entire evidence and the material circumstances relied on by the trial court, disagreed with its assessment, and explained its conclusion that the case against the appellants had been proved.
The High Court's appraisal and conclusion were not erroneous on the record.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to reassess the evidence and reach its own conclusion; it did not err in reversing the acquittal and convicting the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principles stated in Sanwant Singh v. State of Rajasthan, [1961] 3 S.C.R. 120, and applied in Rambhapala Reddy v. State of A.P., A.I.R. 1971 S.C. 460, an appellate court has full power to review the evidence in an appeal against acquittal. The approach in Sheo Swarup v. King-Emperor, 61 I.A. 398, remains a guide. The appellate court must consider the entire record, including the trial court's reasons, bear in mind the presumption of innocence and the fact of acquittal, and state why the acquittal was not justified. Expressions such as 'substantial and compelling reasons' do not curtail that power. Bansidhar Mohanty v. State of Orissa, A.I.R. 1955 S.C. 585, was also considered.

rule.if: state_appeal_against_acquittal and appellate_court_reviewed_entire_evidence and appellate_court_considered_trial_court_reasons and appellate_court_accounted_for_acquittal_and_presumption_of_innocence and appellate_court_explained_why_acquittal_was_unjustified

predicates.state_appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding was a State appeal against an acquittal.
predicates.appellate_court_reviewed_entire_evidence: The appellate court examined the entire body of evidence.
predicates.appellate_court_considered_trial_court_r: The appellate court considered the material circumstances and reasons on which the trial court based its acquittal.
predicates.appellate_court_accounted_for_acquittal_: The appellate court bore in mind the initial presumption of innocence and the fact that the accused had been acquitted.
predicates.appellate_court_explained_why_acquittal_: The appellate court stated reasons for concluding that the acquittal was not justified.
predicates.appellate_court_may_reach_its_own_conclu: The appellate court may review the evidence and reach its own conclusion about guilt.

issues.definition: When an appellate court in a State appeal against acquittal reviews the whole record, considers the trial court's reasons and the effect of the acquittal, and explains why it was unjustified, it may reach its own conclusion about guilt.

issues.legal_issue: Interference under Article 136 is not justified when the challenged appellate conviction reflects a proper appraisal of the evidence and the conclusions are not shown to be so erroneous as to warrant intervention.
material_facts: The accused sought special leave to appeal against convictions imposed by the High Court after it allowed the State's appeal against acquittal.

The Supreme Court considered the High Court's appraisal of the evidence and the criticism of the investigation, including the site-plan allegation, and found no error or sufficiently grave suspicion warranting a different conclusion.

The Supreme Court was not persuaded that the High Court had departed from the principles governing appeals against acquittal or that its conclusions were otherwise sufficiently erroneous to justify intervention.
issues.conclusion: There was no ground for interference under Article 136, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution, interference was not warranted on the arguments raised because the High Court had properly appraised the evidence, had not failed to follow the principles governing appeals against acquittal, and had not reached conclusions shown to be sufficiently erroneous. The Court considered and applied Sanwant Singh v. State of Rajasthan, [1961] 3 S.C.R. 120, Rambhapala Reddy v. State of A.P., A.I.R. 1971 S.C. 460, and Bansidhar Mohanty v. State of Orissa, A.I.R. 1955 S.C. 585.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_conviction_on_: The proceeding was a special-leave appeal against a conviction entered after a State appeal against acquittal.
predicates.high_court_properly_appraised_evidence: The High Court properly assessed the evidence and relevant circumstances.
predicates.no_failure_to_follow_acquittal_appeal_pr: The High Court did not fail to follow the principles governing appellate review of an acquittal.
predicates.no_sufficiently_erroneous_conclusion_sho: The appellant did not show that the High Court's conclusions were so erroneous as to warrant intervention.
predicates.supreme_court_does_not_interfere: The Supreme Court does not interfere with the challenged decision.

issues.definition: In a special-leave appeal from a conviction entered after a State appeal against acquittal, proper evidentiary appraisal and no sufficiently serious error mean that the Supreme Court does not interfere.
